title: Cross-language streaming cursor semantics, retry/backoff policy, and graceful-degradation SDK contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD: Define a stable, language-agnostic contract for streaming cursors, pagination tokens, retry/backoff semantics, and graceful-degradation behavior that Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs will implement. Goal is to reduce customer regressions during runtime upgrades, make cursor semantics debuggable across languages, and provide a clear deprecation/migration path for future cursor format changes.
scope_changes: Initial scope covers read-only streaming endpoints (chat/generation and embeddings stream), stateless pagination tokens for list APIs, and client-side retry/backoff conventions. Excluded: bidirectional streaming for WebSocket integrations, server-initiated resumption tokens for async jobs. If we later adopt encrypted cursors for on-prem deployments, that will be a follow-up feature under Private SDK work.
decisions: Cursors will be opaque to applications but parsable by SDKs for diagnostics (formatted with a short version prefix).
Cursor format chosen: 'v2|<kind>|<base64-opaque>|<short-hmac>' to allow forward-compatible parsing and quick rejection of incompatible versions.

Retry policy default: exponential backoff with jitter, max 6 retries for idempotent list/embeddings calls, max 2 retries for single-shot generation streaming handshakes. SDKs expose a configurable RetryPolicy object mapped to language idioms.

Streaming resume semantics: SDKs must support resuming a stream from a cursor token where server supports resume; in degrade mode, SDKs fall back to starting a fresh stream and emit a 'resumed_as_fresh' telemetry event.
Backward compatibility: SDKs will accept v1 and v2 cursors for 18 months; v1 acceptance will log a deprecation warning once per client process for observability.
Telemetry: SDKs must surface telemetry events for cursor parse failures, retry saturation, and resume fallbacks (allowing customers to opt-out).
acceptance_criteria: Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs implement the v2 cursor parser and can generate v2 cursors when requested by the client surface.

Cursor token round-trip test: server issues v2 token -> SDK resumes stream -> server accepts and returns identical continuation sequence in 100% of CI runs across all three languages in synthetic tests.
Pagination tokens for list APIs remain opaque strings; SDKs provide type-safe iterators that accept the opaque token and expose a stable next() interface across languages.
Retry semantics documented and enforced: default retry/backoff matches PRD policy; SDKs include a configurable hook to override RetryPolicy with unit tests covering override behavior.

Streaming handshake failure: SDKs attempt defined retry counts and emit clear errors when exhausted; integration tests simulate transient network errors and ensure client-side retries do not cause duplicate side-effects for idempotent APIs.

Graceful degradation behavior validated: when resume is not supported or signature mismatch occurs, SDK emits a 'resume_failed_start_fresh' event and application continues with a fresh stream; end-to-end tests confirm data continuity behavior expectations.
Compatibility matrix established and automated: matrix includes Python 3.10+, Node 18+, Go 1.20+; CI runs sample resume and pagination scenarios on each runtime.
Migration guide drafted and published with code snippets for all three languages showing how to opt into v2 cursors and detect v1 deprecation warnings.
Performance regression checks: adding cursor parsing must not increase cold-start latency by more than 8ms median in SDK microbenchmarks for each language.
Security review: cursor HMAC short-sig design reviewed by security team and approved or cataloged as an action item prior to GA.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): release SDKs with v2 cursor support behind explicit opt-in flag and detailed migration docs; collect telemetry for two weeks. Phase 2 (canary): enable v2 generation by default for 10% of new customers and monitor resume success and warnings. Phase 3 (GA): enable by default, deprecation window for v1 begins with 18-month notice and server still accepts v1 but logs. Provide backport shims for customers on older runtimes. Coordinate with runtime/serving team for concurrent server support and rollout.
